name: Microsoft Olive (Onnx LIVE) - hardware-targeted ONNX optimization / quantization composer
bits: not a single format: Olive runs search over conversion + quantization passes and emits whichever ONNX quant configuration wins for the declared target. Quantization algorithms were expanded in Olive 0.8.0 (2025-03) and again in 0.9.2 (2025-08)
activation_scheme: target-dependent; NPU support arrived in Olive 0.9.0 (2025-05)
kernels: Olive emits an ONNX graph + external data; the runtime kernels are ONNX Runtime's, not Olive's
per-tensor / per-channel quantization configs searched against a latency+accuracy constraint
quality_delta: n/a - no quality delta published. Null + note.
notes: PROXY ENUM VALUE - DECLARED 2026-10-04 (already partially self-declared, now explicit): Olive is a search orchestrator whose quant format is an OUTPUT of a hardware-targeted search, filed under 'int8'. The record deliberately declines to claim a group size or bit width because the format is not an input to the tool - but the scheme field still asserts INT8, which is the one thing the record explicitly refuses to claim. This is an inconsistency between the notes and the enum within a single record. REQUESTED ENUM ADDITION: 'olive'. GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 by design: Olive is a search orchestrator whose quant format is an OUTPUT of a hardware-targeted search, not an input. The record already states it deliberately declines to claim a group size or bit width. Nothing to read. EXISTS (MIT, ~2.4k stars, 2k+ commits) and is NOT a quantizer in the llama.cpp sense - it is a search orchestrator. Its own framing, quoted: 'Given a model and targeted hardware, Olive composes the best suitable optimization techniques to output the most efficient ONNX model(s) for inferencing on the cloud or edge, while taking a set of constraints such as accuracy and latency into consideration.' So the quant format is an OUTPUT of a search, not an input, and the record deliberately does not claim a group size or a bit width - null rather than a guess. WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING even with those nulls: it is the Microsoft-side answer to 'which quant should I pick', it is the tool the ONNX Runtime ecosystem expects to sit between a PyTorch checkpoint and an ORT session, and it is where NPU targets enter the picture (Olive 0.9.0, May 2025). Its own quickstart installs `transformers onnxruntime-genai` together, and the docs ship an Olive blog specifically on exploring optimal quantization settings for small language models (Oct 2025). SCOPE CAVEATS: examples moved to a separate olive-recipes repository in Sep 2025; and the ONNX Runtime GenAI builder README explicitly lists 'Olive integration' as still PENDING, so the two do not yet compose. quantization_record is a null-scheme-leaning record by design.
